root.name: King's Gambit Declined: Zilbermints Double Countergambit

overview: Black replies 2...g5 to the King's Gambit, a double countergambit with pawns on e5 and g5 both attacked by White. White can take 3.fxg5 or 3.fxe5, and Black tries to use the open lines and ...Qh4+ or ...Qxe4+; I am not sure of the theory. Material is likely to be unclear at first but Black is probably worse with best play.

white_ideas.idea: Take on g5 or e5 and consolidate with d4 and Nf3
Develop quickly and punish Black's loosened kingside

typical_structures.structure: Open King's Gambit structure with advanced g and e pawns

character.notes: Both kings are exposed and play is forcing.

gambit.notes: Black offers pawns in a countergambit and White can keep them.

soundness.notes: It is a rare line thought to be unsound.

structure.notes: Open lines, e- and f-files open early.

approach.notes: Almost never played by strong players.

level.notes: Dubious so not Beginner; some theory.

character.reason: A countergambit with both kings exposed.

gambit.reason: Black plays 2...g5 offering a pawn that White can keep.

soundness.reason: Black's early pawn offer weakens the kingside with little in return.

structure.reason: Open lines in the centre and on the kingside.

level.reason: Dubious so not Beginner, but the line has little depth.

plans.reason: Black seeks activity and open lines against the White king.
